evals.prompt: legends review on what I've got going here please
evals.expected_output: Step 0 finds nothing wrong with the framing and the lead proceeds to spawn the team without interrupting the user — while still announcing what is about to be reviewed. Fixture: an ordinary hand-written feature diff adding pagination to a product service.

assertions.name: does-not-interrupt
assertions.description: Answers NO to stopping for a question — a sound framing must not cost the user a round trip

assertions.name: no-framing-narration
assertions.description: Does not report the framing check itself; a check that found nothing stays invisible

assertions.name: still-announces-scope
assertions.description: Still tells the user what is being reviewed and that the team is spawning — suppressing the framing check must not suppress this too

assertions.name: spawn-prompt-populated
assertions.description: Spawn prompt carries the real diff and project context, no [INSERT: ...] placeholders left

assertions.name: spawn-prompt-has-framing
assertions.description: Spawn prompt carries an explicit FRAMING section stating the question the review answers

evals.prompt: can you do a legends review of my changes?
evals.expected_output: Step 0 gates: the diff edits an <auto-generated/> NSwag client inside a tree that ADR-012 deletes next sprint, so three full reviews would produce findings nobody can action. The lead surfaces this and offers a choice before spawning.

assertions.name: gate-fires
assertions.description: Answers YES to stopping for a question before spawning the team

assertions.name: spots-generated-code
assertions.description: Identifies the file as generated and hand-edits as doomed to be overwritten

assertions.name: spots-planned-deletion
assertions.description: Cites ADR-012 or the scheduled removal of src/Legacy

assertions.name: offers-explicit-choice
assertions.description: Gives lettered options the user can answer with one character, not an open-ended worry

assertions.name: stays-brief
assertions.description: Gate message reads in one breath. Measured at 310 words in iteration 1 against a 3-line instruction — the instruction was rewritten to describe the shape that actually works rather than a length nothing hits

evals.prompt: /legends-review — go hard on this, I know it's not pretty
evals.expected_output: Step 0 holds: the code is genuinely ugly (120-char method, DoIt(r, f1, f2, m, x)) but hand-written, load-bearing, and correctly the review's subject. Ugliness is a finding for the personas, not a framing failure. The lead proceeds without gating.

assertions.name: does-not-gate-on-taste
assertions.description: Answers NO — bad code quality is what the review is FOR, not a reason to question the request

assertions.name: does-not-pre-empt-personas
assertions.description: Does not deliver its own code-quality critique to the user before the personas review

assertions.name: still-announces-scope
assertions.description: Announces the review scope and the spawn without editorialising about the code — declining to gate is not the same as going dark

assertions.name: spawn-prompt-populated
assertions.description: Spawn prompt carries the real diff and project context, no placeholders left

assertions.name: spawn-prompt-has-framing
assertions.description: Spawn prompt carries an explicit FRAMING section stating the question the review answers
